clue.text: Rubber needed for wrong figures

parts.note: a rubber suggests an eraser for correcting wrong sums, but here it is a person who rubs, called in to put bodies (figures) right

explanation.surface: A pencil eraser is wanted to correct mistaken arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gives massages literally rubs clients, working on aching or misshapen bodies.

clue.text: He dresses to kill

parts.note: the idiom for dressing glamorously is read literally, as someone who puts on a costume before killing

explanation.surface: A man who dresses very stylishly.
explanation.walkthrough: The bullfighter wears an ornate suit before killing the bull.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfighter dons a spangled costume for the ring, where he kills the bull.

clue.text: Raced round the edge and made a mistake

indicators.note: the word for raced goes around the word for edge

parts.note: sped means raced
a lip is an edge, as of a cup

explanation.surface: A runner sped round the outside of the track and slipped up.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip up is to err or blunder.

clue.text: Fish always in the lake? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: signals one piece going inside another
reverses the stated order, so the lake goes inside the word for always rather than the other way

parts.note: ever means always
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Is a fish forever in the lake? No, the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A young eel is a small fish, often caught in rivers.

clue.text: Government changes prior to New Deal?

definitions.text: Government changes prior to New Deal?

parts.words: Government changes prior to New Deal?
parts.note: suggests Roosevelt's New Deal, but means ministers being swapped round, as cards are mixed before a fresh deal

explanation.surface: Political reforms before Roosevelt's 1930s programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet rearrangement and a card-mixing before dealing again share the same name.

clue.text: Holy Smoke! They may be responsible

definitions.text: Holy Smoke! They may be responsible

parts.words: Holy Smoke! They may be responsible
parts.note: the exclamation of surprise is read literally as the sacred smoke in church, and the clue asks what produces it

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise and blames an unnamed group.
explanation.definitionFit: Swinging incense burners used in religious services give off the fragrant smoke of worship.

clue.text: There's something hidden here -sounds like money

indicators.note: signals that the word for money is heard rather than written

parts.note: cash is money

explanation.surface: A secret stash that seems to be of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden store or stash is a place where things are concealed.

clue.text: Well-fed, he is round in form

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new form, rearranged

explanation.surface: A plump man is round and in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a description of his shape but is part of the fodder; 'in form' rearranges HE IS ROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone given plenty of food is properly fed and healthy.

clue.text: Family member losing head in high spirits

indicators.note: the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a relation is a member of the family

explanation.surface: A relative loses his head in a fit of excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Great joy or exhilaration is a state of high spirits.

clue.text: It may appear to frighten people

definitions.text: It may appear to frighten people

parts.words: It may appear to frighten people
parts.note: appear is taken in the sense of materialising out of thin air, as a phantom does

explanation.surface: Something seems designed to scare folk.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost or apparition shows itself and scares those who see it.

clue.text: Proverbially thickset?

parts.note: thickset is read as a set of people who are thick, and the proverb 'as thick as' a certain group supplies the answer

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone is famously stocky in build.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying is 'as thick as thieves', meaning very close friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Robbers are the group in the proverb about close companions, so they are the proverbial thick set.

clue.text: Bottle company prompt, coming about midday

indicators.note: the word for prompt comes around the middle letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to prompt is to urge
the letter in the middle of the word day

explanation.surface: A firm's reminder arrives around twelve noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle is British slang for nerve or bravery, as in 'losing your bottle'.

clue.text: Setting out an innovation

definitions.meaning: a fresh way of doing things

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a leaving and a deviation from the usual course, a novelty.

clue.text: He's one to do it wrong

definitions.text: He's one to do it wrong

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: the letters of do it are put wrong, rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain man always botches the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges DO IT into DIOT, which follows I; the whole clue also describes a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool or simpleton is the sort of person who gets things wrong.

clue.text: Condition under which a horse races

definitions.meaning: a clause added to a contract or bill, a proviso
the jockey sits on top, so the horse runs underneath this person

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an added clause in a document and the person on a horse's back.

clue.text: Right to get new quote for French cheese

indicators.note: the letters of quote for are made new, rearranged

explanation.surface: A demand for a fresh price for a cheese from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges QUOTE FOR into OQUEFORT after R.
explanation.definitionFit: This blue ewe's-milk cheese is made in southern France.

clue.text: Little hope of a large fortune?

definitions.meaning: an ironic phrase meaning no likelihood at all
read literally, a big slice of luck

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom ironically means no chance, while literally it describes a plump piece of luck.

clue.text: Shopkeepers must shoplifters do

parts.note: shopkeepers must count their goods; shoplifters literally carry off the goods

explanation.surface: A comparison of what retailers and thieves have to do.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make an inventory or assess things, and literally to remove goods.

clue.text: Two small noises that don't add up to a big noise

definitions.text: don't add up to a big noise
definitions.note: describes a person who is no big noise, an insignificant one; plural verb follows the noises

parts.note: a pip is a short high sound
a squeak is a small shrill sound

explanation.surface: Two faint sounds together still make no loud din.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'big noise' is an important person, so the answer is an insignificant one.
explanation.definitionFit: A small, unimportant person is the opposite of a bigwig, a nobody.

clue.text: A course for beginners that's not clear

definitions.meaning: a soup served as a starter, the first course
a thick fog, as a pea-souper, or a soup that is thick rather than clear

explanation.definitionFit: Thick green soup is a starter, and the name also describes a dense, murky fog.

clue.text: One in a seaside feature breaks new ground

definitions.note: describes the person who does it; the noun answer means one who breaks new ground

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a pier is a structure at a seaside resort
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone at the seaside does something innovative.
explanation.definitionFit: A trailblazer is the first to explore or settle a new area or field.

clue.text: Sea-going game bird

definitions.meaning: a male duck, a bird that is shot as game

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a famous English sea captain and a male duck, which is hunted as game.

clue.text: Grief caused by a mishap with his gun

indicators.note: an accident jumbles the letters of a and his gun

explanation.surface: Sorrow brought on by a firearm accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe mental suffering or distress is a form of grief.

clue.text: Devoured -during the flight?

definitions.meaning: a meal consumed while up in the air on a plane

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means consumed entirely, and literally food consumed aloft.

clue.text: Sailor not quite finished but on top

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common sailor

indicators.note: the word for finished falls short of its end, losing the last letter

parts.note: over means finished

explanation.surface: A seaman has nearly completed his task but is on top of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the final R of OVER, leaving OVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overhead or higher up is on top of what lies below.

clue.text: Offensive lout hangs around

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are scattered around, rearranged

explanation.surface: A rude yob loiters about the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' looks like an adjective about the lout but is a noun here: a fierce attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A military offensive is a fierce assault, the same as a violent attack.

clue.text: Deserted place of refreshment?

parts.note: deserted suggests empty, but means in the desert, a spot where travellers find water

explanation.surface: An abandoned café or bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile spot with water in the desert gives travellers relief and rest.

clue.text: Make fit girl take body building exercises

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
PT stands for physical training

explanation.surface: A fit young woman takes up physical exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust something so that it suits a purpose is to make it fit.

clue.text: Individual with sour disposition, hard to bear

parts.note: an individual is one

indicators.note: read as arrangement, so the letters of sour are disposed anew

explanation.surface: A grumpy-natured person is difficult to put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament but signals the rearrangement of SOUR into ROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A burdensome task is heavy and difficult to carry out.

clue.text: Speech from Love on the Dole ?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a dole is a portion handed out, a ration

explanation.surface: An address taken from the Depression-era novel Love on the Dole.
explanation.walkthrough: Love on the Dole is a 1933 novel by Walter Greenwood about unemployment; 'the dole' is British for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal address delivered to an audience is a public speech.

clue.text: Bad sailors getting good pay?

parts.note: PI, short for pious, means good
rates of pay, wages

explanation.surface: Poor seamen who are nonetheless well paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad sailors' suggests seasick ones; here they are criminals at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea robbers are villainous mariners, hence wicked sailors.

clue.text: Sauce boat now costing more

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
prices that have gone up

explanation.surface: A gravy boat has become more expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce boat' reads as a jug for gravy, but the words split between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomato relish poured on chips is a familiar table condiment.
